hyps.why: Replacing a parameter-free pool with a 3x3 conv on the output edge gives large gains, unlike upgrading a 1x1 conv.
An already-learnable 1x1 conv leaves little to gain from the upgrade.
Removing edge 0 when edge 1 is none severs the node 1 path and collapses accuracy.
A strong conv alternative path via node 1 cushions the loss of edge 0.
Replacing the direct input-to-output skip with a conv hurts, whereas replacing a 1x1 conv is mostly beneficial.
Swapping a heavy 3x3 conv for a skip on the direct edge improves gradient flow and removes redundancy.
Replacing a 3x3 conv with a skip on the output edge loses capacity, more than replacing a 1x1 conv.
Upgrading a skip to a 3x3 conv adds capacity, while replacing a 1x1 conv yields about nothing.
Without an edge 3 route the network has weaker alternative paths and benefits less from a stronger edge 0.
With a skip carrying the direct path, adding conv capacity on edge 4 helps consistently.
